user_stories.story: As a user, a rule I create is only acknowledged (201) once it is durably stored in Postgres, so it survives restarts.
As a user, listing rules shows what is actually in Postgres, newest first, bounded by a limit, optionally filtered by symbol.
As a user, deleting a rule removes it from Postgres first; 404 if it does not exist.
As an operator, when Postgres is missing or down the app stays up (health, tick ingestion) and rule endpoints answer 503 instead of silently pretending to succeed.
As an operator with an old volume, existing rules are preserved when the obsolete NOT NULL webhook_url column is dropped at startup.
As a developer, CI exercises the rule persistence against a real Postgres, while a plain local pytest still passes offline.

changes_by_file.file: - Define a dedicated exception (e.g. DatabaseUnavailable) raised when the pool is None or rule persistence is disabled (rules_persistence_enabled=False counts as "no DB" for rule endpoints). - save_rule(rule): INSERT only; raises on unavailable or any DB error. No logging-and-swallow. (Duplicate id is not a real case; ON CONFLICT upsert may be kept or dropped.) - delete_rule(rule_id) -> bool: True if a row was deleted, False if no row; raises on unavailable/DB error. - New list_rules(symbol: Optional[str], limit: int) -> list[Rule]: SELECT ... [WHERE symbol=$1] ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT n; raises on failure. Use a deterministic tiebreak (id) after created_at. - load_rules(): still returns all rules for startup; may raise; the caller handles it. - SCHEMA: after CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS alert_rules, run ALTER TABLE alert_rules DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS webhook_url during connect(), so existing rows are kept. Keep column set otherwise unchanged (created_at stays DOUBLE PRECISION). - connect() behaviour on failure unchanged (log, pool=None, app keeps running). The tick path / enqueue_tick is untouched. - Update module docstring (no longer "best-effort" for rules).

- RuleStore stays the evaluation copy only. Its load() at startup: on any repo failure or DB unavailable, log and leave the store empty (no raise). Provide a way for the router to add a rule object and discard by id in memory only after the DB call succeeded (e.g. put(rule)/discard(id)); RuleStore must no longer perform persistence in add/remove. RuleStore.add(data) may remain as an in-memory-only helper because test_rules_engine.py uses it with RuleStore(). - RuleStore.list() no longer used by the API.

- POST: build Rule from RuleCreate, await db.save_rule(rule); on any exception return 503 and do not touch memory; on success add to memory and return 201 with the Rule. - GET: query params symbol (optional, normalized via normalize_symbol, invalid -> 422) and limit (int, default 50, ge=1, le=500, out of range -> 422); call db.list_rules; any exception -> 503. Response model list[Rule], same keys as today. - DELETE: await db.delete_rule(id); exception -> 503; False -> 404; True -> remove from memory, 204. - 503 body: JSON with a detail message that contains no connection string or credentials.

- No behavioural change to on_tick or lifespan, except that startup must not fail when the DB is unavailable (already true; confirm rule_store.load swallows). db remains injectable via create_app(db=...).

- Add an in-memory FakeDatabase (e.g. tests/fakes/fake_db.py) implementing the same rule methods (save_rule, delete_rule, list_rules, load_rules, connect, close, enqueue_tick no-op, available) with a switch to make rule methods raise. The default `client` fixture injects it so existing rule tests keep passing; add a `client_no_db`/failing variant. - Fast offline tests (tests/test_api_rules.py): 201 shape; POST with failing fake -> 503 and memory (rule_store) unchanged and later GET after recovery does not show it; GET ordering newest first, limit honoured, limit=0/501/abc -> 422, symbol filter normalized, bad symbol 422; DELETE 204, 404 unknown, 503 on failing fake with memory unchanged; real default Database with database_url="" -> all three endpoints 503 and /health 200. - Update test_rules_engine.py::test_store_crud_and_persistence_errors_are_swallowed to match the new RuleStore contract (load swallows errors; store no longer persists). - New backend/tests/test_rules_postgres.py (real Postgres): module-level skip with explicit reason when env TEST_DATABASE_URL is unset (e.g. "TEST_DATABASE_URL not set; real-Postgres tests skipped"). Fixture truncates/drops alert_rules (and ticks) before each test so every test starts clean. Tests: save/list/delete round trip incl. ORDER BY created_at DESC, limit, symbol filter, delete returns False for missing; migration test that pre-creates alert_rules with webhook_url TEXT NOT NULL and one stored row, runs Database.connect(), asserts the column is gone and list/load returns the row; unavailable-DB path (bad URL) raises from rule methods; API round trip POST->GET->DELETE via create_app(settings with database_url=TEST_DATABASE_URL, upstream_factory=FakeFinnhubClient.factory); a restart test (two lifespans, rule from first is returned by second). - Settings in tests are always built with _env_file=None and explicit values; Finnhub key empty; FakeFinnhubClient used. Nothing touches Finnhub.
- In the backend pytest step add env TEST_DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:ci_only_password@localhost:5432/ticks (same service; may keep DATABASE_URL). Real-DB tests must run, not skip, in CI.
- Unchanged unless the existing client surfaces rule errors in a way that breaks on 503; if so, minimal handling only. npm run build and npm test must still pass.

acceptance_criteria.c: From backend/ with TEST_DATABASE_URL unset, pytest passes; the real-Postgres tests are reported as skipped with a reason mentioning TEST_DATABASE_URL.
With TEST_DATABASE_URL pointing at an empty Postgres 16, pytest passes and the real-Postgres tests run (0 skipped from that module).
POST /api/rules with a working DB returns 201, body keys exactly id, symbol, type, threshold, window_seconds, created_at, symbol uppercased; the row exists in alert_rules and in the in-memory store.
POST with a DB that raises, or with no DB configured, returns 503; the in-memory RuleStore is unchanged (verified by test) and the response body leaks no URL/credentials.

GET /api/rules returns rows from Postgres ordered by created_at DESC; limit defaults to 50; limit=1 and 500 accepted; limit=0, 501, non-integer -> 422; symbol filter (case-insensitive) works; invalid symbol -> 422; DB failure/no DB -> 503. GET never reads the in-memory store (test: a rule added only to memory is not returned).
DELETE /api/rules/{id}: existing -> 204 and gone from Postgres and memory; unknown id -> 404; DB failure/no DB -> 503 and memory unchanged.

With the backend started with no DB: POST/GET/DELETE /api/rules all return 503, GET /health returns 200, and ticks are still processed (on_tick does not raise, rule engine still evaluates memory rules).
With a real DB: POST a rule, restart the app (new lifespan), GET returns the rule, and the RuleEngine fires it on a matching tick (memory reloaded via load_rules).

A pre-existing alert_rules table having webhook_url TEXT NOT NULL and one row: after Database.connect() the column no longer exists (information_schema check), a new POST succeeds (no NOT NULL violation), and the old row is returned by GET.
Database rule methods raise on failure (no swallowing): save_rule/delete_rule/list_rules on an unavailable Database raise; delete_rule returns False for a missing id.
Startup with an unreachable or unset DB does not raise; the rule store starts empty.
Services.on_tick and Database.enqueue_tick are unchanged in behaviour (non-blocking, no awaits on Postgres).
ci.yml sets TEST_DATABASE_URL for the backend pytest step pointing at the service container; frontend npm run build and npm test pass.
No test touches Finnhub; each real-DB test begins with clean alert_rules (and ticks).

assumptions.a: rules_persistence_enabled=False is treated like "no DB" for the rule endpoints (503), since the DB can no longer be bypassed.
The existing default `client` fixture (database_url="") would now return 503 for rules, so it is changed to inject the fake DB; a separate fixture covers the no-DB case.
created_at stays DOUBLE PRECISION (epoch seconds), so ORDER BY created_at DESC works unchanged; ties broken by id for determinism.
Real-DB tests use asyncpg directly (already a dependency) and the existing pytest-asyncio auto mode; the test DB is disposable and tests may drop/truncate alert_rules and ticks.
A GET with symbol and limit applies the filter before the limit.
503 is used for every DB failure, including mid-run connection loss; no retry/reconnect logic is added.
Rule persistence failures are not retried; the client is expected to retry.
Dropping the webhook_url column is idempotent and runs on every connect.

edge_cases.e: DB goes down after startup: POST/GET/DELETE return 503; memory evaluation copy keeps working for already-loaded rules.
DB insert succeeds but response never reaches client: rule exists in DB and memory; acceptable.
DELETE of a rule present only in memory (not in DB): 404, memory left as is (documented limitation, should not occur).
Concurrent POSTs: each gets a unique id; no interference.
Rule with window_seconds NULL (price rules) round-trips as null.
limit boundary values 1 and 500; symbol filter with whitespace/lowercase; empty symbol param treated as no filter (current behaviour).
Schema fix runs on a fresh DB (no webhook_url column) without error; run twice without error.
Startup load_rules failure (query error) is logged without credentials and leaves an empty store.

risks.risk: Changing the default test client to a fake DB and RuleStore's contract touches existing tests (test_rules_engine store test); must be updated without weakening engine coverage.
If the DB is down at startup but returns later, the memory store stays empty (no reload) so persisted rules will not fire until restart. Accepted by user decision 2; mention in docs/notes.

Real-DB tests share a database with a developer's data if TEST_DATABASE_URL points at a live DB; tests drop/truncate tables, so the variable must target a disposable DB. Add a clear note in the test module docstring.

Event-loop interplay between pytest-asyncio tests and TestClient in the API round-trip test; keep the API real-DB tests synchronous (TestClient) and DB-method tests async, with separate connections for setup/cleanup.
CLAUDE.md invariant 7 conflicts with real-Postgres tests; the orchestrator updates it (out of scope for implementer).

spec.dependencies: asyncpg (existing), pytest-asyncio (existing, asyncio_mode=auto), FastAPI TestClient, Postgres 16 service in CI (existing), env var TEST_DATABASE_URL.
spec.out_of_scope: watchlist/latest_prices/alerts tables, browser websockets, rate limiting, auth, dependency pinning, fail-loud startup; no edits to CLAUDE.md or revised-planning.md.
spec.self_critique: Every story maps to a criterion (create=3,4; list=5; delete=6; outage=7,11; migration=9; CI=1,2,13,14). All criteria are observable via HTTP status, DB inspection or pytest skip reports. Biggest remaining risk: the exact fake DB interface and RuleStore refactor are implementation choices that could break test_rules_engine.py if mishandled, and the memory-empty-after-late-DB-recovery gap, which the user decisions accept. No blocking ambiguities found.
